name: CryoET Data Portal (Chan Zuckerberg Biohub / CZ Imaging Institute)
what: 3D cryo-electron tomograms of frozen cells and organelles, with labelled objects (points, oriented points, segmentation masks); objects named by GO cellular component or UniProt accession

access.bucket: s3://cryoet-data-portal-public (public HTTPS listing works from here; us-west-2)
access.api: GraphQL via the cryoet-data-portal Python client (endpoint not reachable from this sandbox)
access.formats: MRC / OME-Zarr tomograms (multiple GB each), ndJSON points, MRC / Zarr masks, JSON metadata

terms: Terms of use: publicly available, provided as is, no re-identification; no data licence stated -> treat as local only, cite Ermel et al. 2024 Nat Methods 21:2200 (doi:10.1038/s41592-024-02477-2) and the dataset authors

labelled_objects_in_human_cells (first 3: cytosolic ribosome and membrane-bound ribosome (HEK293, HSC-3 unroofed plasma membranes)

richest_whole_cell_labels: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (ribosome, proteasome, F1-F0 ATP synthase, CCT chaperonin, RubisCO, ER, mitochondria, nuclear envelope); S. pombe (ER, mitochondria, microtubules, fatty acid synthase)
scan_note: objects scanned in the first run of 356 of 392 datasets (connection dropped near the end); membranes are labelled in 329 of them
use_for_cellbrain: only direct evidence of assembled machines in place (limit 7, 'is the machine built'), but human labels today are thin (ribosomes in 2 lines, actin in RPE1); Jurkat and RPE1 tomograms exist unlabelled for machines, so machines would need picking with a particle-finding model on a GPU
